finding: A rebased fix now counts as made only when its stable patch id equals a commit the branch made, so any rebase that changes the fix's patch refuses land with the false reason that no commit was made on the branch. Probed against real git: a rebase onto a moved feature tip with a conflict the developer resolves, the same through `git pull --rebase`, a squash of two own commits in `rebase -i`, and a `--fixup` commit folded by `rebase -i --autosquash` are all refused by 831e743d; the pre-delta function (4d21bcaa) accepted all four.
why: The designed path for a moved tip is a rebase: "A moved tip → one rebase, every tier again, push" (docs/afk/small-lane/SDD.md:365) and "Fixed --> Rebased: tip moved" (docs/afk/small-lane/adr/design/0006-feature-branch-fix-lands-by-fast-forward-push.md:20). A rebase onto a tip that touched the same lines conflicts, and resolving it changes the patch id, so the designed path now ends in a refusal whose reason ("was made on") is untrue.
fix: Identify a replayed own commit by something a rebase keeps: author name, e-mail and author date (`git log --no-walk=unsorted --stdin --format=%H%x00%an%x00%ae%x00%ad`), which survive conflict resolution, reword, squash and fixup (squash keeps the first commit's author), while replayed foreign commits keep their own authors' dates. Keep the patch-id match as a second way in, or drop it. Add tests for a rebase with a resolved conflict and for a fixup folded by --autosquash.
evidence: skills/afk/fix/scripts/ship.py:679-680 `own = set(_patch_ids(cwd, made).values())` / `made |= {c for c, p in _patch_ids(cwd, replayed).items() if p in own}`. Probe <scratch>/r8ds-probe/test_probe8.py, output <scratch>/r8ds-probe/out8.txt: "=== C rebase with conflict resolved by developer ... reflog: 94356318... rebase (finish): refs/heads/fix/bug-export-drops-row onto 11d683e7... / 43943da7... commit: add fix.txt ... result={'step': 'land', 'status': 'refused', 'reason': 'none of the 2 commits past the Base commit 285cb4c2... was made on fix/bug-export-drops-row, so land would ship no fix'}"; same refusal for "C2 pull --rebase with conflict resolved", "F squash two own commits in rebase -i", "F2 fixup + rebase -i --autosquash". Same four cases with the 4d21bcaa function (<scratch>/r8ds-probe/out8-old.txt): "=== C rebase with conflict resolved by developer / result={'step': 'land', 'status': 'done', ...}", and 'done' for C2, F and F2.

criterion: Happy-path-only (Meszaros) / mutation probe: survived mutant on a delta line
finding: No test pins the rule that a merge commit has no patch id. A mutant that gives merges their first-parent diff (`--diff-merges=first-parent` in place of `--diff-merges=off`) passes all 16 rebase and land-kind tests, and with it land answers `done` for a branch whose only made commit was a hand-finished merge that a later rebase dropped, so land ships no fix.
why: skills/afk/fix/scripts/ship.py:646 "Commit id -> stable patch id; a merge or an empty commit has none."; ship.py:656-658 "a replayed commit the branch never made counts for nothing." The only merge test (test_ship.py:1060) uses `git merge --no-ff -m`, whose reflog action is not in MADE_HERE, so no merge ever reaches `_patch_ids`.
fix: Add a test where the branch's only made commit is a merge: checkout -B at the feature tip, moved_feature, `git merge -q --no-ff --no-commit origin/{FEATURE}`, `git commit -q -m ...` (reflog `commit (merge)`), `git rebase -q {start}`; assert HEAD == moved, land refused with "was made on", remote tip unchanged, entries == []. Probe-verified: passes on 831e743d, fails on the first-parent mutant.

Dropping `--diff-merges=off` outright is an equivalent mutant on git 2.53 (`log -p` shows no merge diff by default; probe no_diff_merges_off: 16 passed, candidate passed too).

finding: Each `(finish)` entry re-runs `git log -p` and `git patch-id` over every commit in `made`, and `made` grows by every replayed generation, so the cost grows with commits times rebases. On a branch with 150 commits and 15 rebases the check took 48.4 s (30 `git log` calls, the largest 5.2 s on about 92 KB of commit ids) against 6.3 s for the pre-delta function on the same repository.
why: Each call is bounded by `GIT_TIMEOUT = 300` (skills/afk/fix/scripts/ship.py:74) but nothing bounds their number, so a long-lived branch reflog makes land slower with every rebase while the answer only needs patch ids of commits not yet hashed.
fix: Hash each commit once: keep a dict sha -> patch id across the loop and pass `_patch_ids` only the shas not yet in it, or add only the newly made commits' ids to `own`. The author-identity match proposed in delta-sweep-001 removes the patch-id calls altogether.
